passage: Thank you all for signing up to volunteer with our rural education program this summer. Before we go further, let me explain what the program actually involves. You'll be placed in small groups of four, teaching basic English and mathematics to elementary school students in mountain villages for two weeks, starting the second Monday of July. Accommodation and meals are provided free of charge, but you'll need to cover your own transportation to the meeting point in the city. Please note that this is not a paid position, but volunteers who complete the full two weeks will receive a certificate that many universities recognize for community service hours. Because you'll be working with young children, all volunteers must attend a mandatory training session next Saturday, covering child safety and basic teaching methods. If you can't attend that session for a genuine reason, please email us immediately, as missing it without notice will result in losing your spot to someone on the waiting list.
stem: What is the main purpose of this briefing?
options: To explain details of a rural education volunteer program
To recruit paid teachers for a school
To announce a change in university admissions
To collect donations for village schools
explain_zh: 講者一開始就說明志工計畫的細節,所以目的是說明偏鄉教育志工計畫的內容,不是招募支薪老師、公布入學政策或募款。

passage: Good morning, and welcome to the fifteenth annual Conference on Educational Technology. It's an honor to open this year's event, which has attracted over three hundred researchers from twenty-two countries, our largest turnout yet. This morning's keynote will focus on how artificial intelligence is reshaping personalized learning, followed by a panel discussion at eleven featuring four experts from both academia and industry. Before we begin, a few housekeeping notes: lunch will be served in the main hall from twelve thirty, and please remember that all sessions in the east wing require the badge you received at registration. For those presenting posters this afternoon, setup begins at one, and you'll have until one forty-five before visitors start arriving. Wifi details are printed on the back of your name badge. Finally, this year we've moved to a fully paperless format, so please download the conference app if you haven't already, as printed schedules will not be available at the information desk.

Opening remarks for an academic conference
An announcement of new admission rules

passage:
A: Hi, I'd like to schedule an appointment with a school counselor. I've been feeling really stressed about my exams lately.
B: Of course, thanks for reaching out. Is this your first time visiting our counseling center?
A: Yes, it is. I wasn't sure if I needed a referral from a teacher or something.
B: No referral needed, students can book directly. Our earliest available slot is this Thursday at two, or if that doesn't work, we have one next Tuesday at ten.
A: Thursday works better for me. How long does a typical first session last?
B: The first session usually runs about fifty minutes, a bit longer than regular follow-up sessions, since we'll go over some background questions together.
A: That's fine. Is everything I say kept confidential?
B: Yes, completely, unless there's a serious safety concern, in which case we're required to involve a parent or teacher.
A: I understand. One more thing, is there a fee for this?
B: No, counseling services are free for all enrolled students.
stem: Why does the student want an appointment?
options: She wants to change her class schedule
She is having trouble with a friend
She has been feeling stressed about exams
She needs help choosing a major
explain_zh: 學生一開始就說 I've been feeling really stressed about my exams lately,所以是因為考試壓力,不是排課、交友問題或選系。

passage: Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for attending this session on the Global Futures Scholarship for studying abroad. This scholarship covers full tuition and a monthly living allowance of twenty-five thousand dollars for one academic year at one of our thirty partner universities overseas. Unlike many other scholarships, this one does not require a specific major, but applicants must maintain a GPA of at least three point six throughout their studies here. The selection process has three stages: a written application, a language proficiency test, and finally a panel interview conducted entirely in English. Last year, out of around two hundred applicants, only fifteen students were selected, so competition is genuinely tough. If you're selected, you'll be expected to attend a mandatory pre-departure workshop in June, and upon your return, share your experience through at least two campus presentations. Applications open next week and remain open for exactly one month, so please don't wait until the last minute to prepare your documents.
stem: What does this scholarship cover?
options: Full tuition and a monthly living allowance
explain_zh: 講者說 this scholarship covers full tuition and a monthly living allowance,所以包含學費和每月生活費,不是只有機票或一次性補助。

passage: Today's lecture introduces the ethics of artificial intelligence, a topic that's becoming increasingly relevant as AI systems make decisions that affect real people's lives. One major concern is algorithmic bias, where a system trained on unbalanced data ends up treating certain groups unfairly, even without anyone intending it to happen. A well-known example occurred in twenty eighteen, when a hiring algorithm used by a major company was found to favor male candidates, simply because it had been trained mostly on resumes from men over the previous ten years. Beyond bias, we also need to consider transparency: many advanced AI systems make decisions in ways that even their own developers cannot fully explain, which raises questions about accountability when something goes wrong. Some researchers argue that companies should be legally required to explain how their algorithms reach important decisions, particularly in areas like lending, hiring, and criminal justice. Today, we'll examine three proposed frameworks for addressing these issues, starting with the concept of algorithmic auditing.
stem: What is this lecture mainly about?
options: How to build a hiring algorithm
explain_zh: 講者一開始就說 introduces the ethics of artificial intelligence,所以主題是AI倫理議題,不是程式設計歷史、如何打造演算法或自動化的經濟效益。

passage: Today we turn to a growing concern in space exploration: space debris. Since the launch of the first satellite in nineteen fifty-seven, humans have sent thousands of objects into orbit, and many of them are now broken, unused, or simply forgotten. Current estimates suggest there are over thirty thousand pieces of debris larger than ten centimeters currently orbiting Earth, travelling at speeds of around twenty-eight thousand kilometers per hour. At that speed, even a small piece of debris can seriously damage a working satellite or spacecraft on impact. This became a real-world problem in two thousand nine, when a defunct Russian satellite collided with an active American communications satellite, destroying both and creating thousands of new fragments. Scientists are now developing several solutions, including nets and harpoons designed to capture large debris and pull it back into the atmosphere, where it burns up safely. However, funding for these cleanup missions remains limited, since no single country or company wants to bear the full cost alone.

options: How rockets are launched into orbit

passage: This lecture looks at an often overlooked form of pollution: ocean noise. Unlike plastic waste, which we can see, noise pollution is invisible, but it has a serious impact on marine life, particularly whales and dolphins, which rely on sound to communicate, navigate, and find food. Since the nineteen fifties, background noise in the ocean has roughly doubled every decade, largely due to increased shipping traffic, oil drilling, and sonar equipment used by the military. Studies show that some whale species have had to raise the volume of their calls by as much as twenty-nine percent just to be heard over the noise, which requires significantly more energy. In extreme cases, loud sonar tests have been linked to mass whale strandings, where dozens of whales become confused and swim onto beaches. Some countries have begun creating quiet zones in busy shipping lanes, where ships must reduce speed and noise output during certain seasons, especially when whales are migrating through the area.
stem: What is this lecture mainly about?
options: Noise pollution in the ocean and its effects on marine life
The history of the shipping industry
explain_zh: 講者一開始就說 an often overlooked form of pollution: ocean noise,所以主題是海洋噪音汙染,塑膠汙染只是用來對比,不是主題本身。
